DisputeCorrectionIn.description:
The Organizer's correction of a disputed match, and why.

The fields are ``create_match``'s, except that a scoring type or game
target left out is the disputed match's; a missing best-of is inferred
from the games. The reason is stored in the match's audit log, which
cannot be erased, so it should not name a player.

EventCreateIn.description:
A new Event for a verified Organizer the signed-in Account is a
member of.

``organizer`` and ``club`` are OPEN Codes, in any case, with or
without hyphens. The Club, when named, must have granted the
Organizer a Club Organizer Grant (ADR 0021).

EventKind.description:
The match type of matches recorded with an Event.

Each Match stores the kind it was recorded with, so a kind change
reaches only matches recorded after it (ADR 0035).

The values are the engine's ``open_engine.MatchType`` values.
``self_reported`` is left out: self-reported matches have no Event
(decision F1 in #1). Never add a value the engine lacks.

EventUpdateIn.description:
Changes to an Event. Only the fields sent change; null is refused.

``kind`` may change at any time and reaches only matches recorded
after it (ADR 0035). ``name``, ``start_date``, and ``end_date`` change
only while no match names the Event. The organizer and club cannot be
changed here.

One invalid input: where it is, what kind of error, and a message.

`existing_code` is the earlier match's OPEN code. Only a duplicate match
item has it, and only when the submitter may know that match.

GameOut.description: One game's number and the points each team won.

GameScoreIn.description: One game's score: the points each team won.

The points a game is played to (decision F15 in #1).

The values are the points in the engine's ``ALL_GAME_FORMATS``.

HoldOut.description:
A held match the signed-in Account may vouch for (#270, ADR 0034).

``match`` is the match as the Account sees it. The other match of each
possible duplicate flag that holds it is never named. ``vouched`` is
true when the Account's own level has vouched for this match on every
open flag that holds it: for an Event match, its organizer; for a
match with no Event, a player on the Account's team.

MatchCorrectionIn.description:
A player's correction of a self-reported match (#267).

The same fields as a submission. The teams must be the match's own two
teams, in either order. A missing game target or scoring type is the
corrected match's, and a missing best-of is inferred from the games.

MatchCreateIn.description:
A player's own match submission.

The field names are ``validate_match``'s argument names, so its issues
name the request fields. A missing game target means 11, a missing
scoring type means side-out, and a missing best-of is inferred from
the games. Each team takes at most ``MAX_TEAM_ENTRIES`` codes and the
games at most ``MAX_GAME_ENTRIES`` scores.

MatchFormat.description:
Singles or doubles.

The values are the two base values of ``open_engine.RatingFormat``. The
engine's doubles categories (mixed, men's, women's) are not stored here:
the engine adapter (``apps.ratings.engine_adapter``) derives them from
the players.

MatchOut.description:
A match, its teams, and its games, as the signed-in Account sees it.

``my_team`` is the viewer's own team, null when the viewer's Player did
not play in the match. ``my_decision`` is the latest confirm, dispute,
or withdraw this player recorded on the match, ``none`` when they
recorded none or did not play. A repeated decision is not recorded
again, so confirming again after a dispute that the Event's verified
organizer resolved still shows ``dispute``. An organizer's confirmation is not a player
decision: a player who confirms as a member of the match's Event
Organizer still shows ``none``. For a participant, ``confirmed_by_team``
says whether a player on each team recorded a confirmation (a dispute is
not a confirmation); it is null for anyone else. A confirmation still
shows in ``confirmed_by_team`` after the same player disputes, and
after they withdraw that dispute, since a recorded decision is never
removed: a player who confirmed, disputed, then withdrew shows
``withdraw`` while their confirmation stays in ``confirmed_by_team``.
It counts player confirmations only: a match confirmed by an organizer,
or a correction, can be confirmed with both false, so
read ``status`` for whether the match is confirmed. ``created_at`` is when the match was submitted.

MatchStatus.description:
Where a Match is in confirmation.

Only ``record_match`` (the initial status) and the services in
``apps.matches.workflow`` set it.

One of the signed-in Account's own Organizer memberships.

``organizer`` is the Organizer's OPEN Code, the value
``EventCreateIn.organizer`` takes. ``name`` is the Organizer's name,
shown only to its own members. ``verified`` says whether the Organizer
is verified; it does not say whether the Account may act for it now
(Organizer authority also needs MFA, ADR 0043). ``role`` is the
Account's own role there. It names no other member.

OrganizerReportIn.description:
A report of a verified Organizer to OPEN Moderators.

``reason`` is one of the listed reasons. There is no free text.

The report just made: the Organizer's OPEN Code, the reason, and

PlayerCreateIn.description:
A new Player for the signed-in Account.

``birth_year`` and ``birth_month`` take JSON integers only: a boolean,
a numeric string, or a float is refused, as ``Player.clean_fields``
refuses them.

The body is read only when the session holds no details from signup
(ADR 0017, ADR 0019, ADR 0022): ``display_name``, ``birth_year``,
``birth_month``, and ``gender_division`` are then required. Held
details are used instead of every field here: the held name ("First
Last") becomes the legal name and, for an adult, the display name (a
player aged 13 to 17 starts with "First L."), with the held city and
region. ``gender_division`` is ``mens`` or ``womens``.
Optional text fields left out or null are empty. Unknown keys are
refused.

delete.description:
Delete your Account and your personal data.

Reauthenticate first, through allauth's `auth/reauthenticate` (your
password) or `auth/2fa/reauthenticate` (a two-factor code); without a
recent one you get 403 with code `reauthentication_required`. Your
email address, name, birth year and month, gender division, city and
region, privacy settings, sessions, two-factor methods, and
organizer memberships go. Matches you played stay in the ledger, with
your player shown as a private player, so other players' ratings do
not change. Every session of the Account ends, this one included.
The same email address can sign up again afterwards. A staff or
superuser Account gets 409. An Account that must use two-factor
authentication sets up a method first (403 `mfa_required`).

403.description: Forbidden. Code `mfa_required`: an Account that must have two-factor authentication (staff, superusers, moderators, and owners of a production application) and has none, or an Account with it whose session did not pass it, such as a password-only session. It can still use allauth's endpoints to set it up or sign in with it.

429.description: Too many requests. Retry after the seconds in Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the request can be allowed again: when the refusing limit resets, or when a later limit that is already used up resets.

Correct a pending or disputed match you played in with no Event.

Give the corrected match as for a new one, with the same two teams in
either order. The match is voided and the correction is created
pending, submitted by you and with your confirmation, and returned. It
counts once a player on the other team confirms it. A scoring type or game target left out
is the corrected match's, and a missing best-of is inferred from the
games. Its location, labels, and order come from the corrected match. A
confirmed match gets 409: dispute it first. Anyone who did not play in
the match, a match with an Event or Club, and a correction with other
teams get 404, as for an unknown code.

Dispute a match you played in.

A disputed match stops counting. For a match with an Event, the
Event's organizer then settles it. You can withdraw your dispute
(``/withdraw-dispute``), and for a match with no Event you can
correct it yourself (``/correction``).

Disputing again changes nothing, also after you withdrew your dispute. A voided match cannot be disputed
(409). Anyone who did not play in the match gets 404, as for an
unknown code.

post.description:
Vouch that a held match is not a duplicate of the other match.

A match recorded with the same teams and date as another, with other
scores, is held from counting along with that match until each one is
vouched for at its own level. A match with an Event is vouched for by
a member, with two-factor authentication, of the verified organizer
that ran it whose player is in no match of the match's correction
chain. A match with no Event is
vouched for by one player of each team. A match with a club and no
Event has no level: nobody vouches for it, and a hold against it ends
only when a match is voided or the hold period ends. Once both
matches are vouched for, each counts again once it is confirmed and
no other open hold keeps it. The response is this match only: the
other match is never named. A vouch cannot be undone. Vouching again
records nothing new unless another hold has opened on the match since.
A voided match, and a match nothing holds (a released one included),
get 409. Anyone else gets 404, as for an unknown code.

no dispute is open, it is confirmed again when it was confirmed before
the dispute, else pending, and a confirmed match counts again. Your
dispute still counts as your one dispute, so disputing again changes
nothing. Withdrawing again changes nothing unless the match was voided
meanwhile. A voided match, and a match you have no open dispute on,
get 409. Anyone who did not play in the match gets 404, as
for an unknown code.

post.description:
Create the signed-in Account's Player.

The Account's own email address must be verified (403 otherwise), and
an Account has one Player (409 for a second). Every value comes from
the details held at signup in this session (ADR 0017, ADR 0019, ADR
0022), the held name as the legal name and, for an adult, the display
name (a player aged 13 to 17 starts with "First L."); the body is used
only when the session holds none, and its display name, birth year and
month, and gender division are then required. The held details are
removed once the Player exists (on a 409 too), so a create refused for
any other reason can be retried. A player under 13, or a birth year
and month in the future, is refused with a fixed 422, and the refusal
holds for the session, as at signup: every later create in it gets the
same 422, and so does a signup after logout (ADR 0017).

Upload a CSV results file for an Event of your verified Organizer.

The file is in the CSV results format (``docs/csv-format.md``), at
most 1 MiB and 1000 match rows. ``players_13_or_older`` must be true:
it confirms that every player in the file is 13 or older (422
otherwise, checked before anything else). ``game_target`` (11, 15, or
21) and ``location`` apply to every row. Anyone who may not manage the
Event's matches gets the same 404 as an unknown Event. A larger file
gets 413. The file is processed in the background: the response is
202 with the file pending, and ``get_results_file`` shows the report.
Only the good rows are recorded. A row that repeats a match already
recorded, a pending one included, is reported as a duplicate.
